title: Playing off the beat
summary: Accent the "and" instead of the beat, and the rhythm starts to dance.

steps.title: Syncopation
steps.body:
Playing a note on an "and" and holding it over the next beat, instead of landing on the beat, is **syncopation**. It puts the accent where you don't expect it.

**Why it matters:** It is what makes funk, reggae, Latin music and most modern pop groove. Without it, rhythms sound stiff.

steps.title: Count it first
steps.body: 1, then the "and" of 2, then the "and" of 3, then 4.

items.prompt: Tap on 1, the "and" of 2, the "and" of 3, and on 4: 4 taps.
Tap on 1 and on the "and" of 2, holding it: 2 taps.

steps.title: Push the chord
steps.body: Play C on beat 1, then play the next chord early, on the "and" of 4. That push is everywhere in pop.

items.prompt: Tap on 1, the "and" of 2, the "and" of 3, and on 4: 4 taps.
